Which of the following statements are valid in connection with Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy (2023)?

src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
s: Oxidation process means
x: Oxidation is the loss of electrons (it takes place at the anode); gain of electrons is reduction.

s: Which of the following devices converts chemical energy into electrical energy?
x: An electric cell turns chemical energy into electrical energy by a redox reaction. A heater, fan and hair dryer only use electrical energy.

s: A device which converts chemical energy into electrical energy is called –
x: A battery converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy. A motor converts electrical to mechanical energy, and a generator mechanical to electrical.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Which of the following would most likely have near zero pH value?
x: Battery acid (dilute sulphuric acid) is strongly acidic with a pH of about 0-1. Pure water is 7, milk about 6.5, and saline water about neutral.

s: Alternate current is not preferable –
x: A storage battery can only be charged with direct current, so AC is first rectified to DC. AC is fine for motors, toasters and power transmission.

s: When two or more cells are connected to each other by opposite terminals, then it is called as …… .
x: Two or more cells joined by opposite terminals make a battery. A bulb, a switch and a current are not combinations of cells.

s: The working of a dry cell is based on
x: A dry cell is a galvanic cell. It gives current through a spontaneous oxidation-reduction reaction, while electrolysis needs outside energy.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding a motor car battery.

I. The voltage is usually 12
V.

II. Electrolyte used is hydrochloric acid.

III. Electrodes are lead and copper.

IV. Capacity is expressed in ampere hour.
Which of the above statement are correct ?
x: A car battery is a 12 V lead-acid battery rated in ampere-hours. It uses sulphuric acid, not hydrochloric acid, and lead/lead dioxide electrodes, not copper, so only I and IV are correct.

s:
Assertion (A) : A dry cell cannot be charged.
Reason (R) : Dry cell has a reversible reaction.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
x: A dry cell cannot be recharged because its chemical reaction is irreversible. So A is true and R, which calls the reaction reversible, is false.

s: In dry cell, which of the following are used as electrolytes?
x: The dry (Leclanché) cell uses a moist paste of ammonium chloride and zinc chloride as electrolyte, with a zinc can and a carbon rod with MnO2.

s: In dry cell, which of the following are used as electrolytes?
x: A dry cell uses a paste of ammonium chloride and zinc chloride as electrolyte. Sodium, calcium and magnesium chlorides are not used.

s: Nickel-Cadmium (Ni-Cd) battery is used in :
x: Rechargeable Ni-Cd batteries (nickel oxide-hydroxide and cadmium, KOH electrolyte) powered calculators, cordless appliances and transistors, so 'all of the above' is correct.

s: Which one of the following pairs of materials serve as electrodes in chargeable batteries commonly used in devices such as torchlights, electric shavers etc.?
x: Rechargeable torchlight and shaver batteries are nickel-cadmium cells. Zinc-carbon cells cannot be recharged, and lead peroxide/lead is the car battery.

s: Traditional ‘battery’ contains which of the following chemicals?
x: The traditional lead-acid battery uses sulphuric acid as electrolyte. Ethylene glycol is antifreeze, and sodium bicarbonate and ethanol are not battery chemicals.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020

x: A fluorescent tube holds low-pressure mercury vapour (with argon); the mercury emits UV, which the phosphor turns into visible light.

s: Indiscriminate disposal of used fluorescent electric lamps causes mercury pollution in the environment. Why is mercury used in the manufacture of these lamps?
o: A mercury coating on the inside of the lamp makes the light bright white
When the lamp is switched on, the mercury in the lamp causes the emission of ultraviolet radiations
When the lamp is switched on, it is the mercury which converts the ultraviolet energy into visible light
None of the statements given above is correct about the use of mercury in the manufacture of fluorescent lamps
x: When the lamp is on, mercury vapour emits ultraviolet radiation, and the phosphor coating turns that UV into visible light. Mercury itself does not convert UV to light.

s: The most commonly used substance in fluorescent tubes are –
x: Fluorescent tubes contain low-pressure mercury vapour and argon (sometimes neon, krypton or xenon). Sodium vapour is used in street lamps.

s:
Assertion (A) : Light Emitting Diode (LED) lamps offer longer service life as compared to Compact Fluorescent Lamps (CFL).
Reason (R) : Light Emitting Diodes (LED) lamps are more energy efficient as compared to the Compact Fluorescent Lamps (CFL).
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) explains (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explains
x:
Books/keys: both true, R explains A. Strictly, an LED's longer life comes mainly from its solid-state design (no filament or electrodes to wear out), so R is at best a partial explanation (general knowledge, not checked).
LEDs last longer and are more energy efficient than CFLs. Books key R as the explanation, since LEDs waste less energy as heat.

s: Full form of C.F.L. is –
x: CFL stands for Compact Fluorescent Lamp; it uses about 75% less energy than an incandescent bulb.

s: Sodium Vapor Lamp is usually used as street light, because –
o: Light from this is monochromatic and will not split
It is pleasing to the eyes
x: Low-pressure sodium lamps give monochromatic yellow light that is not split by water droplets or fog, so it suits street lighting.

s: A common fluorescent tube contains ……… .
x: A common fluorescent tube contains mercury vapour; argon is only a buffer gas, and sodium and neon are used in other lamps.

s: Which among the following is most helpful in energy savings?
x: LED bulbs have the highest efficacy and longest life, so they save the most energy. Incandescent bulbs waste most input as heat.

s:
What is the difference between a CLF and an LED lamp?

I. To produce light, a CLF uses mercury vapour and phosphor while an LED lamp uses semiconductor material.

II. The average life span of a CFL is much longer than of and LED lamp.

III. A CFL is less energy- efficient as compared to an LED lamp.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
x: A CFL uses mercury vapour and phosphor while an LED uses a semiconductor (I true), and a CFL is less efficient than an LED (III true). II is false because LEDs, not CFLs, last longer.

s: These days yellow lamps are frequently used as street light. Which one of the following is used in these lamps :
x: Yellow street lamps are sodium vapour lamps. Neon glows red, and hydrogen and nitrogen are not lamp fills for street lights.
